learning_objective: 🎯 Travel back to Ancient Greece and forward to the Modern Olympics to discover the values of excellence, friendship, and respect that unite the world!

key_vocabulary.hindi_meaning: मंच (विजेताओं के खड़े होने का स्थान)

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Started in 776 BCE in the valley of Olympia, Greece, in honor of the Greek god Zeus. They were abolished in 393 CE. Only Greek men were allowed to participate.
Revived by Baron Pierre de Coubertin, a French educator. The first Modern Olympics were held in Athens, Greece, in 1896. He believed sports could promote international peace and understanding.
The Olympic flag has five interlocking rings (Blue, Yellow, Black, Green, Red) representing the union of the five continents. At least one of these colors appears in the flag of every nation.
The traditional motto is 'Citius, Altius, Fortius' (Faster, Higher, Stronger). In 2021, the word 'Communiter' (Together) was added to highlight solidarity.
Olympism is a philosophy of life. It teaches three core values: Excellence (doing your best), Respect (for rules, yourself, and others), and Friendship (building global harmony).

fun_activity.title: 💍 Design the Rings
fun_activity.instructions: Take five different colored pens: Blue, Yellow, Black, Green, and Red. Try to draw the Olympic rings exactly how they interlock on the flag (Top row: Blue, Black, Red. Bottom row: Yellow, Green). It's harder than it looks!

exam_tips: 📌 Always credit 'Baron Pierre de Coubertin' as the father of the Modern Olympic Games.
📌 Memorize the updated Olympic Motto: Citius, Altius, Fortius – Communiter (Faster, Higher, Stronger – Together).
📌 Know the primary bodies: IOC (International Olympic Committee) organizes the games globally, and NOCs (National Olympic Committees) manage teams for specific countries.
quick_recap: ⭐ The Ancient Olympics featured events like chariot racing, wrestling, and the pentathlon.
⭐ The Olympic flame symbolizes the light of spirit, knowledge, and life.
⭐ Olympism blends sport with culture and education to build a better world.
